title: The generic-rank conjecture for bipartite circulant graphs
source: Daniel Irving Bernstein, Grigoriy Blekherman and Rainer Sinn, Typical and Generic Ranks in Matrix Completion, arXiv:1802.09513, Conjecture 5.6 (Linear Algebra and its Applications, 2020). (https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.09513)
statement:
Let $G(n,l)$ be a bipartite circulant graph of the form considered in the paper, and let the generic completion rank be the rank attained by a generic matrix completion. The dimension-count prediction is

$$
n-
\left\lfloor\sqrt{n^2-nl}\right\rfloor.
$$

**Bipartite circulant generic-rank conjecture.** Every graph $G(n,l)$ has generic completion rank predicted by the dimension count; equivalently,

$$
\operatorname{gcr}(G(n,l))=n-\left\lfloor\sqrt{n^2-nl}\right\rfloor.
$$

The paper proves the dimension-count prediction for a subset of these graphs and conjectures it for all bipartite circulant graphs of this form. The claim is presented as unresolved.
summary: For all n > 0 and 0 <= l <= n, the bipartite circulant graph G(n, l) has generic completion rank n - floor(sqrt(n(n - l))), the value predicted by the dimension count. This is Conjecture 5.6 of Bernstein, Blekherman and Sinn, who proved it for special families and named the step that was missing. The upper bound uses a new construction: Fourier vectors with an evenly spaced (Beatty) set of frequencies, so that each frequency class has at most d elements, and a Vandermonde system on the missing diagonals that forces the tangent map to be injective. The lower bound is the dimension count. Lean states generic completion rank literally, as a statement about a nonempty Zariski-open set of partial matrices in both directions, and proves the passage from a nonzero Jacobian minor to such an open set.
paste_summary: Proved. Every bipartite circulant graph G(n, l) has generic completion rank n - floor(sqrt(n(n - l))), as predicted by the dimension count. This is Conjecture 5.6 of Bernstein, Blekherman and Sinn (arXiv:1802.09513), which the source proves only for special families.
caveat: Bounded literature search only. Cross-model confidence: correct 0.98, not public 0.85, not routine 0.75, Lean statement equals the printed conjecture 0.97. The printed formula omits a ceiling; the Lean formula n - Nat.sqrt(n(n - l)) equals the dimension-count prediction the conjecture names (checked for n <= 12). Closest later work: Dressler and Krone, arXiv:2010.09777, on real typical ranks of the same graphs, which does not prove the complex formula.
